title: Derived residue homology detects a nonzero rank-one stalk coefficient
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], E an object of its derived module category [def-pc-derived-category], a: O_S[0] → E and s ∈ U. Let P be strictly perfect on the localized module site [def-pc-perfect-complex], with zero terms in negative degrees. Fix e: E|_U ≅ Q(P), c: (O_S[0])|_U ≅ Q(A), where A is the single restricted structure sheaf, and α: A → P with Q(α) = c⁻¹ ≫ a|_U ≫ e. Assume H⁰(Li_s* a) is invertible for the residue morphism i_s and derived pullback [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-derived-pullback]. For any linear isomorphisms σ: A⁰_s ≃ O_{U,s} and τ: P⁰_s ≃ O_{U,s}, the residue of τ(α⁰_s(σ⁻¹(1))) in κ(s) is nonzero. Stalks are computed via the over-site equivalence and the module stalk functor.

proof.text: Apply lem-sc-residue-stalk-homology-map-comparison to obtain IsIso of the degree-zero homologyMap of α after the over-site equivalence, module stalk, and residue scalar extension.

Both differentials into and out of degree zero of the single source vanish, even after applying the residue stalk functor. Thus its cycle inclusion and homology quotient are isomorphisms. Naturality of homologyπ shows cyclesMap is mono when homologyMap is mono; naturality of iCycles then makes the degree-zero component mono. This is the proved private helper mono_component_of_mono_homology.

Conjugate the stalk map by σ and τ to an R-linear endomorphism g of R, with g(r)=g(1)r. Extension of scalars preserves these conjugating isomorphisms. If res(g(1))=0, tensor balancing makes every image 1⊗g(r) zero, so scalar extension of g is zero. Since it is mono its source is zero. But 1⊗1 in κ⊗R maps to 1 under the tensor right unitor, contradicting nontriviality of the residue field. This is the proved helper residue_coefficient_ne_zero_of_mono, and establishes the unchanged conclusion.
